title: Passage and Rivergate
premise: Gideon Yarrow, a bush pilot who fled a family scandal by vanishing into the interior, is hired to resupply an archaeological expedition up the Rivergate. When the team goes silent, he flies in against his own rules and finds them decimated by fever and guarding a discovery they refuse to name: proof that Gideon's presumed-dead father led a previous expedition into the same gorge twenty years ago—and never came out. To bring the survivors home before the river floods, Gideon must navigate rapids no plane can cross, decide what to do with evidence that would rewrite his family's history and destroy another man's reputation, and finally choose whether to remain a ghost or become his father's son. He gets three survivors to Rivergate, burns the proof of his father's fate at his own hand, and lands for the first time under his real name.
about_author: Quentin Marchetti is the pen name of a former floatplane mechanic who spent six seasons in remote northern camps before turning to fiction. Passage and Rivergate is his third novel and the first written entirely from memory rather than research.

chapters.title: Ten Thousand Hours of Sky
chapters.summary: Gideon Yarrow flies medicine and mail across the interior, narrating his philosophy of measured miles over lived years. POV: Gideon. Beat: establish competence, isolation, and the quiet dread beneath his routine.

chapters.title: The Manifest
chapters.summary: At Rivergate's dirt strip, Gideon loads supplies for the Halloway expedition—antibiotics conspicuously doubled, a crate marked FRAGILE: DO NOT OPEN. POV: Gideon. Beat: unease seeded; the reader notices what Gideon pretends not to.

chapters.title: Radio Silence
chapters.summary: Nine days later, the expedition misses its scheduled check-in, then two more. The sponsor, Aldous Crane, offers Gideon triple pay to fly upriver and investigate. POV: Gideon. Beat: reluctance versus obligation; the trap of being needed.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Gideon reviews maps of the Rivergate gorge, where his own charts end in blank space labeled only with his father's initials. POV: Gideon, with flashback texture. Beat: the past surfaces as geography.

chapters.title: Crane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Crane reveals the expedition sought a pre-war surveyor's camp; he pressures Gideon with knowledge of the Yarrow name and a sealed file. POV: Gideon. Beat: blackmail disguised as opportunity.

chapters.title: Weather Window
chapters.summary: A storm front gives Gideon forty-eight hours. He strips his plane, takes on fuel drums, and tells himself it's just another charter. POV: Gideon. Beat: commitment made in denial.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: The flight north through building weather; engine trouble forces a landing on a gravel bar short of the camp. POV: Gideon. Beat: control slipping—the sky stops cooperating.

chapters.title: Camp Hollow
chapters.summary: Gideon reaches the expedition site on foot: tents shredded, radio smashed, one member dead of fever, two missing. POV: Gideon. Beat: horror tempered by triage instinct.

chapters.title: The Survivors
chapters.summary: He finds archaeologist Mara Voss delirious and young tech Sam Okafor guarding a sealed strongbox with a rifle. Neither will say what happened. POV: Gideon. Beat: distrust between rescuer and rescued.

chapters.title: Fever Logic
chapters.summary: Mara, lucid in fragments, warns him not to open the box and not to go to the gorge. Gideon recognizes her fear as recognition—she knows who he is. POV: alternating Gideon/Mara. Beat: identity becomes currency.

chapters.title: The Gorge Road
chapters.summary: Against warnings, Gideon hikes to the gorge rim and finds the old surveyor's camp: rusted tools, a cairn, and a ledger bearing Elias Yarrow's handwriting. POV: Gideon. Beat: grief ambushes him mid-investigation.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Lost
chapters.summary: The ledger records his father's 2003 expedition and a find described only as 'the passage.' The final entry trails off mid-sentence. POV: Gideon. Beat: hope and horror entangled.

chapters.title: Sam's Rifle
chapters.summary: Back at camp, Sam confesses the expedition leader tried to take the strongbox downriver alone and drowned; the box holds documents Crane paid them to retrieve—or bury. POV: Sam flashback via Gideon's questioning. Beat: moral fault lines revealed.

chapters.title: Rising Water
chapters.summary: Rain upstream means the river will flood the gravel bar within days, stranding them all. Gideon calculates weight, fuel, and lives. POV: Gideon. Beat: the clock starts audibly ticking.

chapters.title: The Box
chapters.summary: Gideon opens the strongbox alone at night: photographs, a survey map, and a coroner's report suggesting Elias Yarrow survived the 2003 crash—and was left behind. POV: Gideon. Beat: the wound reopened.

chapters.title: Left Behind
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, 2003: young Gideon waits at a radio for a father who never calls in. POV: Gideon (past). Beat: the origin of his mile-counting life laid bare.

chapters.title: Mara's Testimony
chapters.summary: Recovered enough to talk, Mara admits Crane funded the trip to confirm the old man died in the gorge—so his claim on Yarrow land would lapse. POV: Mara. Beat: the conspiracy gains a face.

chapters.title: Fuel Math
chapters.summary: Three survivors, gear, headwinds: the plane can't carry them all from the bar. Someone must stay for a second run that may be impossible. POV: Gideon. Beat: survival priced in arithmetic.

chapters.title: Volunteer
chapters.summary: Sam insists Mara goes first; Gideon quietly plans to stay himself, mirroring his father's final choice. POV: Gideon. Beat: inheritance as self-sacrifice.

chapters.title: First Lift
chapters.summary: Gideon flies Mara out through the storm's leading edge, nearly stalling on the ridge, and lands at Rivergate half-fueled. POV: Gideon. Beat: triumph shadowed by cost.

chapters.title: Crane at the Strip
chapters.summary: Crane meets the plane, asks pointed questions about the box, and offers Gideon money and erasure of his past. Gideon lies smoothly—for the first time choosing what to hide. POV: Gideon. Beat: invisibility weaponized.

chapters.title: The Second Run
chapters.summary: Gideon refuels against the weather officer's warning and heads back; the river has already taken part of the bar. POV: Gideon. Beat: gambler's descent.

chapters.title: Stranded
chapters.summary: He lands on the remaining gravel; Sam is alive but the current has cut off the route to the gorge cache of extra fuel drums. POV: Gideon. Beat: plan collapsing into improvisation.

chapters.title: Raft of Wreckage
chapters.summary: They build a raft from expedition debris to reach the fuel cache upstream. POV: alternating Gideon/Sam. Beat: forced partnership, grudging respect.

chapters.title: White Water
chapters.summary: The raft run through the gorge rapids; they lose a drum and nearly Sam, saved by Gideon's rope work. POV: Gideon. Beat: action peak of the middle act.

chapters.title: The Cave Mouth
chapters.summary: Sheltering from rain, they discover the cave the ledger called 'the passage'—and inside, remains and a field journal proving Elias lived weeks after the crash, repairing a raft. POV: Gideon. Beat: the father rehumanized.

chapters.title: Last Entry
chapters.summary: Elias's journal ends asking whoever finds it to tell his son he wasn't running away—he was coming home. POV: Gideon reading aloud. Beat: catharsis; the theme of inheritance crystallizes.

chapters.title: What to Carry
chapters.summary: Sam argues the journal could ruin Crane publicly; Gideon weighs justice against the dead man's dignity. They load fuel, not vengeance. POV: Gideon. Beat: moral decision deferred but shaped.

chapters.title: Overload
chapters.summary: Weight check: journal, drum, two men—one thing must stay. Gideon leaves his father's compass on the cairn. POV: Gideon. Beat: letting go as literal act.

chapters.title: Climb-Out
chapters.summary: Overloaded takeoff through rain and rising wind; the plane clears the trees by feet. POV: Gideon. Beat: white-knuckle climax of flight.

chapters.title: Intercepted
chapters.summary: Crane's chartered plane shadows Gideon on the radio, demanding he divert and surrender 'company property.' POV: Gideon. Beat: antagonist closes in.

chapters.title: Dead Stick
chapters.summary: Fuel starvation forces Gideon to glide to a logging clearing; Crane's man waits on the ground with a pistol and a purchase offer. POV: Gideon. Beat: standoff at zero altitude.

chapters.title: The Price Named
chapters.summary: Gideon refuses to trade the journal for his anonymity; the man hesitates—then Mara arrives with the regional police, tipped by Sam's satellite message. POV: Gideon. Beat: allies strike back; villain's leverage breaks.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: In Rivergate, Mara and Sam give statements; Crane's funding fraud unravels. Gideon declines to testify about his father, keeping one thing private. POV: Mara. Beat: justice partial, chosen.

chapters.title: Grounded
chapters.summary: The damaged plane is grounded for repairs; Gideon, idle for the first time in years, faces stillness and the question of his name. POV: Gideon. Beat: aftermath discomfort.

chapters.title: Yarrow
chapters.summary: He registers the repair bill and the flight plan under his full legal name—Gideon Elias Yarrow—for the first time since he was nineteen. POV: Gideon. Beat: identity reclaimed in small bureaucratic act.

chapters.title: The Letter
chapters.summary: Gideon writes to his mother enclosing a copy of the journal's last page, keeping the rest. POV: Gideon. Beat: reconciliation attempted at distance.

chapters.title: Recertified
chapters.summary: Inspection passed, Gideon takes the plane up alone at dawn, flying the gorge once—not to look down, but to look along the way home. POV: Gideon. Beat: closure in motion.

chapters.title: Passage
chapters.summary: Epilogue-flavored scene: months later, Gideon carries passengers now, answers to his name, and keeps the empty strongbox as a reminder that some cargo is carried so it can be set down. POV: Gideon. Beat: resolution—survival's price acknowledged, inheritance transformed.

chapters.title: Rivergate
chapters.summary: Final image: the town, the strip, the river running high and ordinary; a new charter request comes over the radio and Gideon says yes. POV: Gideon. Beat: forward-looking ending; the story becomes a life.
